3:102.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِۦ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ
3:102.en: O ye who believe! Observe your duty to Allah with right observance, and die not save as those who have surrendered (unto Him)

3:103.ar: وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِحَبۡلِ ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُواْۚ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذۡ كُنتُمۡ أَعۡدَآءࣰ فَأَلَّفَ بَيۡنَ قُلُوبِكُمۡ فَأَصۡبَحۡتُم بِنِعۡمَتِهِۦٓ إِخۡوَٰنࣰ ا وَكُنتُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفۡرَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ فَأَنقَذَكُم مِّنۡهَاۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
3:103.en: And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate. And remember Allah's favour unto you: How ye were enemies and He made friendship between your hearts so that ye became as brothers by His grace; and (how) ye were upon the brink of an abyss of fire, and He did save you from it. Thus Allah maketh clear His revelations unto you, that haply ye may be guided

3:104.ar: وَلۡتَكُن مِّنكُمۡ أُمَّةࣱ يَدۡعُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡخَيۡرِ وَيَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِۚ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
3:104.en: And there may spring from you a nation who invite to goodness, and enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency. Such are they who are successful

3:105.ar: وَلَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُواْ وَٱخۡتَلَفُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُۚ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
3:105.en: And be ye not as those who separated and disputed after the clear proofs had come unto them. For such there is an awful doom

3:106.ar: يَوۡمَ تَبۡيَضُّ وُجُوهࣱ وَتَسۡوَدُّ وُجُوهࣱۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡوَدَّتۡ وُجُوهُهُمۡ أَكَفَرۡتُم بَعۡدَ إِيمَٰنِكُمۡ فَذُوقُواْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡفُرُونَ
3:106.en: On the Day when (some) faces will be whitened and (some) faces will be blackened; and as for those whose faces have been blackened, it will be said unto them: Disbelieved ye after your (profession of) belief? Then taste the punishment for that ye disbelieved

3:107.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ٱبۡيَضَّتۡ وُجُوهُهُمۡ فَفِي رَحۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
3:107.en: And as for those whose faces have been whitened, in the mercy of Allah they dwell for ever

3:108.ar: تِلۡكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱللَّهِ نَتۡلُوهَا عَلَيۡكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلۡمࣰ ا لِّلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
3:108.en: These are revelations of Allah. We recite them unto thee in truth. Allah willeth no injustice to (His) creatures

2:132.ar: وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَآ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعۡقُوبُ يَٰبَنِيَّ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ
2:132.en: The same did Abraham enjoin upon his sons, and also Jacob, (saying): O my sons! Lo! Allah hath chosen for you the (true) religion; therefore die not save as men who have surrendered (unto Him)

3:110.ar: كُنتُمۡ خَيۡرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخۡرِجَتۡ لِلنَّاسِ تَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَتَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَتُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ ءَامَنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۚ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَأَكۡثَرُهُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
3:110.en: Ye are the best community that hath been raised up for mankind. Ye enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency; and ye believe in Allah. And if the People of the Scripture had believed it had been better for them. Some of them are believers; but most of them are evil-livers

zO_pgKOXpiU.speaker: adnan
zO_pgKOXpiU.speaker_note: His own khutbah series on the Quran; speaks as the imam people bring conspiracy theories to, addressing his London congregation.
zO_pgKOXpiU.title: Listening to the Divine: Aal-Imran 102-112
zO_pgKOXpiU.one_line: The post-Uhud verses: taqwa by Allah's measure, faith that grows, holding the rope together, commanding good; our problem is internal.
zO_pgKOXpiU.summary: A khutbah on Aal-Imran 102-108 with 3:110, the passage revealed after Uhud that opens every Friday sermon. He argues these verses matter more to Muslims in the West than any other part of the Quran because, whatever conspiracies people bring him, our real problem is internal, as the Prophet foretold when he said the ummah would be many yet weak. He unpacks taqwa haqqa tuqatih as mindfulness measured by Allah's status rather than our ability, which requires knowing Him as He described Himself; dying as Muslims means faith that grows, so anyone who says they were better years ago should read the graph and intervene radically. Holding the rope of Allah all together means collective i'tisam, drowning people gripping the lifeline and each other, which the Quran imposes even though doing it alone would be easier. He recalls Uhud's losses, the Prophet's lasting wounds and the broken treaties, then the favour of enemies made brothers, visible in a congregation of every nationality. Following Ibn Ashur and Ibn Kathir, all of us are meant to be the ummah that calls to good and commands ma'ruf, the social ethics that keep a society alive, against the individualism of these countries. He ends by asking where the output of 30,000 Muslims, a tenth of London, is, and says the mentality has to change.

outline.heading: Opening
Recitation of 3:102-108
outline.gist: He recites the passage from 'fear Allah as He deserves to be feared' to 'Allah intends no injustice to the worlds'.

outline.heading: Why these verses now: the problem is internal
outline.gist: The first half of Aal-Imran deals with challenges from outside the ummah, the second half, revealed after Uhud, with those from within. Despite the conspiracy theories people bring him, the real problem is inside our societies, communities and souls.

outline.heading: The nations around the dish: many, yet weak
outline.gist: The Prophet foretold the nations calling one another against the ummah; asked whether it would be because Muslims were few, he said they would be many. So it was known from the start that numbers would not be the problem, which makes these internal verses more relevant today than any other part of the Quran.

outline.heading: Taqwa haqqa tuqatih: by His measure, as He describes Himself
outline.gist: Taqwa is a specific Islamic term: protect yourself according to the status of the One you fear, not your ability or fear. How much protection that takes depends on knowing Allah as He described Himself in His Book, not as you imagine Him; understanding God is not a personal choice unless you are a prophet.

outline.heading: Do not die except as Muslims
outline.gist: We do not control our deaths; the command is to keep faith growing so that nothing has shaken it when the end comes. Yaqub gave his sons the same instruction in Al-Baqarah.

outline.heading: 'I was better years ago': read the graph
outline.gist: People say they miss when their faith was stronger and are not frightened by it. If it was higher then and lower now, it keeps going down unless you halt everything and intervene radically; a passing thought between busy days is not how this deserves to be treated.

outline.heading: Hold the rope together, not each alone
outline.gist: I'tisam jami'an means holding on as one unit: gripping the rope and each other, like drowning people who share one lifeline and keep hold of the person beside them.

outline.heading: Into the aftermath of Uhud
outline.gist: The verses came after a disaster: prominent companions lost, the Prophet wounded with headaches until his death, neighbouring tribes breaking treaties and killing Muslims, and plenty of people to blame for running or turning back.

outline.heading: Remember the favour: enemies made brothers
outline.gist: Allah joined hearts that had been enemies so that Muhajirin and Ansar stood in perfectly aligned rows. A congregation of different nations, looks and languages carrying one understanding of the Messenger is the same blessing, and He saved them from the brink of the fire.

outline.heading: Together is harder, and there is no other option
outline.gist: Protecting faith collectively is a headache he would rather avoid, but the Quran gives no individual option. When we do not get along, remember that the person beside you comes from a country once at war with yours.

outline.heading: Minkum: all of you, not a few
outline.gist: With Ibn Ashur, Ibn Kathir, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak he reads 'minkum' as explanatory: may all of you be the ummah that calls to good, not a small group among you.

outline.heading: Khayr and ma'ruf: creed and social ethics
outline.gist: Khayr is the shahadah, salah, zakah and hajj; ma'ruf is the socially understood ethics every community needs to keep functioning. Calling to both is how faith is protected and how people succeed.

outline.heading: Do not be like those who divided
outline.gist: 3:105: communities that split into sects, stopped working together, harmed their own and allied with enemies against their own blood and faith face a great punishment.

outline.heading: Whitened and blackened faces
outline.gist: 3:106-108: those who disbelieved after faith taste the punishment, those whose faces shine abide in Allah's mercy, and Allah intends no injustice to the worlds.

outline.heading: Interlude
Why every minbar opens with this verse
outline.gist: In Arabic: imams open every khutbah with 3:102 for its meaning and because the companions knew it came after Uhud, when they felt crushed, ashamed before their Lord and confused; the second half of Aal-Imran healed them.

outline.heading: First the individual, then the nation
outline.gist: Allah begins with the self: taqwa and a heart full of Islam when death comes. Then the collective: i'tisam together, where you may hold a brother who holds the rope. Listen to your Lord's words, not his or anyone else's.

outline.heading: Against individualism: the group sails together
outline.gist: A Muslim who does not call to good or see his society as one body is following the hateful individualism of these lands, which has exhausted them. You have individual value and responsibility, but you succeed only if the group sails.

outline.heading: The best nation brought out for people
outline.gist: 3:110: the goodness of this ummah is meant to spread to others; commanding good, forbidding wrong and believing in Allah bring benefit to the whole community.

outline.heading: Imam Ahmad: a strong leader with less piety
outline.gist: Asked which leader to prefer, Imam Ahmad chose the strong one with less piety: the pious man's piety is his own while his weakness falls on the people; the other's sin is his own while his strength serves them.

outline.heading: 1926 and 2026: see the change in people
outline.gist: For the first time we can compare footage across a century instead of trusting historians; look at how people have changed. We cannot afford to lose everything.

outline.heading: Hold each other to what we all agree on
outline.gist: Commanding good means holding one another to shared standards, starting with simple ones like reckless driving and leaving cars in the wrong places. Ignore the bad and fear to speak of the good, and the community slowly deteriorates.

outline.heading: Care for everyone, not just your circle
outline.gist: Whatever afflicts another group will reach yours. The city's Muslims must make sure every child is taught, the weak strengthened, the sick treated and the lost found; the effort, money and plan can only come from the community.

outline.heading: Where is the output of 30,000 Muslims?
outline.gist: London has one of the highest shares of Muslims in North America, a tenth of the city against one or two percent nationally. The numbers are high but the output is missing; the mentality has to change.

outline.heading: Outro

39:42.en: Allah receiveth (men's) souls at the time of their death, and that (soul) which dieth not (yet) in its sleep. He keepeth that (soul) for which He hath ordained death and dismisseth the rest till an appointed term. Lo! herein verily are portents for people who take thought

DPelx-v9sKE.speaker: adnan
DPelx-v9sKE.speaker_note: continues his own Tazkiyah mortality series; speaks of his oncology patients and serving as imam at deathbeds
DPelx-v9sKE.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 27
DPelx-v9sKE.one_line: Prepare for death rather than fear it; live a life you believe in, and use mortality as the one weapon that humbles the nafs.
DPelx-v9sKE.summary: He opens by explaining that tazkiyah is meant to be taught in small doses and closed circles, and urges listeners to absorb rather than merely hear. Recapping, he says life only has meaning against death, and sleep is a minor death in which Allah takes and returns souls. Since death is inevitable, the logical response is preparation, not fear. He tells the story of a Umayyad caliph who, on his last Hajj, asked an elderly scholar why people hate death; the answer was that they built up this world and ruined the next. The scholar's blunt advice led the caliph to bequeath rule to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, showing that even a king can prepare sincerely. From his oncology practice he describes dying patients, often Muslims, who protest that they have not lived yet, which he attributes to living by rules they never believed in; Islam must be experienced as the fullest way to live. He then argues that not knowing our time is a gift, and that mortality is the nafs' kryptonite: the body-bound nafs fears death above all, so accepting mortality is the only tool to tame it. The companions' fearlessness, shown by Rib'i ibn Amir before the Persian commander, came from this, without making them careless about life.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah is taught in small doses
outline.gist: His own teachers spoke for ten minutes on a single line so it could be absorbed; listen again until these ideas become second nature.

outline.heading: Why these topics are kept for closed circles
outline.gist: Tazkiyah needs follow-up and feedback; information heard once and not absorbed can set a person back.

outline.heading: Recap: life is meaningful only against death
outline.gist: Mortality, unlike the moment of death, must be accepted; values, motivation and appreciation of life need its opposite, as sweetness needs sourness.

outline.heading: Sleep as a minor death
outline.gist: Allah takes souls in sleep and returns those whose time remains; children fear sleep for the loss of consciousness it brings.

outline.heading: Not fear, but preparation
outline.gist: A Muslim does not fear nothingness since death is a transition; one may fear the unknown and accountability while also looking forward to meeting Allah.

outline.heading: Preparation is the only logical response
outline.gist: Everyone before and after us dies at a steady pace, so preparing for death becomes the most important task.

outline.heading: A caliph's last Hajj
outline.gist: An aging Umayyad caliph, burdened by his dynasty's bloodshed, asked for anyone in Medina who had met the companions.

outline.heading: The scholar who would not come
outline.gist: Every notable greeted the caliph except one elderly scholar, who said he had no reason to visit someone he did not know.

outline.heading: Why do we hate death?
outline.gist: Because you built up this world and invested nothing in the next; no one wants to move from a mansion to a ruin.

outline.heading: 'What should I do?'
outline.gist: Pressed, the scholar told the caliph his dynasty took power without consultation, shed blood and seized wealth; the caliph silenced his angry courtiers.

outline.heading: The advice and the will to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
outline.gist: Told only someone preparing for death could return stolen wealth and restore consultation, the caliph bequeathed rule to his cousin Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who reformed the dynasty.

outline.heading: Even a king can prepare
outline.gist: No one can say there is nothing they can do; sincere preparation is always possible.

outline.heading: 'I haven't lived yet'
outline.gist: Elderly patients given months to live, including a man on oxygen with his third cancer, beg for more time because they feel they never lived.

outline.heading: Why some Muslims die angry
outline.gist: Non-Muslims who lived as they believed often die calmer than Muslims who lived by rules they never believed in.

outline.heading: Islam is the fullest way to live
outline.gist: If Islam does not feel like the best life to you, you have not understood it yet, and talking about preparing for death is pointless until you do.

outline.heading: A meaningful life brings a calm death
outline.gist: Self-honesty and the 'last week' exercise aim at living as you truly believe; meaningful lives end calmly across the board.

outline.heading: Is not knowing our time a curse or a gift?
outline.gist: Argue both sides; one student argued passionately that knowing would let us repent in time.

outline.heading: Reaching sixty is fair notice
outline.gist: Age and illness give warning, and the Prophet said whoever reaches sixty has no excuse left.

outline.heading: Mortality is the nafs' kryptonite
outline.gist: You cannot beat the nafs without a tool; the spirit returns to Allah and does not fear death, but the body-bound nafs fears it above all because it will not return the same.

outline.heading: Without mortality you are disarmed
outline.gist: Good company and habits are not enough; the nafs will corrupt everything unless reminded of its death.

outline.heading: Near-death liberation and the final boss
outline.gist: After a near miss the cornered nafs falls silent and you think freely until it returns; mortality is the sword for the final boss.

outline.heading: Play the card every day
outline.gist: The Prophet said death is enough as an admonisher; the nafs neutralises it by convincing you to ignore it, so think about death daily to humble it.

outline.heading: Death is not depressing
outline.gist: Returning to Allah and meeting the righteous is not depressing; only the nafs feels that way because it is its end.

outline.heading: Without accountability you will ignore mortality
outline.gist: Rejecting accountability removes the reason to care about death, leaving no power over the nafs and no selfless action.

outline.heading: Rib'i ibn Amir before the Persian commander
outline.gist: Piercing the priceless carpet with his cheap spear, he said his people love death for Allah as much as the Persians love life.

outline.heading: Accepting death means valuing life more

32:15.ar: إِنَّمَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهَا خَرُّواْۤ سُجَّدࣰ اۤ وَسَبَّحُواْ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ۩
32:15.en: Only those believe in Our revelations who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate and hymn the praise of their Lord, and they are not scornful

32:16.ar: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُمۡ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
32:16.en: Who forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope, and spend of that We have bestowed on them

32:17.ar: فَلَا تَعۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ مَّآ أُخۡفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعۡيُنࣲ جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
32:17.en: No soul knoweth what is kept hid for them of joy, as a reward for what they used to do

32:18.ar: أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقࣰ اۚ لَّا يَسۡتَوُۥنَ
32:18.en: Is he who is a believer like unto him who is an evil-liver? They are not alike

32:19.ar: أَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتُ ٱلۡمَأۡوَىٰ نُزُلَۢا بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
32:19.en: But as for those who believe and do good works, for them are the Gardens of Retreat - a welcome (in reward) for what they used to do

32:20.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فَسَقُواْ فَمَأۡوَىٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُۖ كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓاْ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَآ أُعِيدُواْ فِيهَا وَقِيلَ لَهُمۡ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ

32:21.ar: وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَكۡبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ

ieFkmCJj8Oc.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat As-Sajdah (verses 15-21)
ieFkmCJj8Oc.one_line: Seek teachers whose state leads to Allah; the traits of true believers, their hidden reward, and worldly hardship as Allah's call to return.
ieFkmCJj8Oc.summary: He frames everything in Islam as serving the relationship with Allah: prayer comes from connection, and taqwa is one question, whether an act harms that bond. Scholars distinguished deeds from inner states, and a student should accompany someone whose state leads to Allah, not merely someone with information, which any chatbot can supply. He illustrates with Abu Hanifa's careful search for a teacher until he found Hammad, Malik's mother sending him to take Rabi'ah's manners before his knowledge, and Ibn Wahb spending nineteen of twenty years learning adab from Malik. Returning to verses 15-16, he explains falling in prostration as eager descent, arrogance as the destroyer of love, sides that cannot rest in bed, and spending as the practical proof of love, since prayer and zakat stand for worship toward Allah and toward people. The companions were changed by the Prophet's state, as when a rabbi saw his face and believed. Verses 17-21 describe a hidden delight no soul knows, the highest reward being the sight of Allah's face, and the inequality of believer and sinner. The lesser punishment of worldly hardship is sent so people return and are spared the greater one, so no trial should pass without bringing you closer.

outline.heading: Opening
Every act serves the relationship with Allah
outline.gist: Prayer, fasting and avoiding sin all aim at strengthening the bond; salah is linked to connection, as is keeping ties of kinship.

outline.heading: Taqwa as one question; deeds versus states
outline.gist: Taqwa asks whether an act angers Allah and harms the relationship; the scholars asked not only about deeds but about one's state with Allah, a secret no angel or devil can touch.

outline.heading: Accompany one whose state leads you to Allah
outline.gist: Information is available anywhere, even from a chatbot, but it has no state with Allah; a teacher must guide by his condition before his words.

outline.heading: Abu Hanifa searches for a teacher
outline.gist: Al-Sha'bi urged the bright young merchant to study; Abu Hanifa spent months observing scholars' prayer and manners until he settled on Hammad and prayed for him all his life.

outline.heading: Abu Hanifa's generosity to Abu Yusuf
outline.gist: He paid the orphaned student and his mother to study, yet said his own teacher Hammad was more generous still.

outline.heading: Malik: take his manners before his knowledge
outline.gist: Malik's mother sent him to Rabi'ah to learn adab first; Ibn Wahb said he learned knowledge from Malik in one year and adab in nineteen.

outline.heading: Knowledge without closeness only distances
outline.gist: Answers to rulings are worthless if the heart is far and the prayer has no spirit; whoever grows in knowledge but not guidance only grows further from Allah.

outline.heading: Falling in prostration: an eager descent
outline.gist: The restrictive 'only' limits true belief to those who fall swiftly in prostration when reminded, like someone rushing toward a treasure.

outline.heading: Arrogance destroys love
outline.gist: Pride ruins marriages and friendships when neither will reconcile; servitude ('ubudiyyah) was originally one of the Arabs' degrees of love, distinct from slavery.

outline.heading: Sides that cannot rest, calling in fear and hope
outline.gist: Like a restless child, the lover of Allah cannot settle in bed; he fears a just punishment and hopes in a mercy that encompasses all things.

outline.heading: Love without action is acting
outline.gist: One who prays all night but cheats customers and harms his family is performing, not loving.

outline.heading: Prayer and zakat: the two kinds of worship
outline.gist: The Quran pairs them as symbols of worship between you and Allah and worship through serving people; spending completes the description of love.

outline.heading: The Prophet waits for Aisha to sleep
outline.gist: Out of courtesy he asked her leave to rise for night prayer, and answered that he wished to be a grateful servant.

outline.heading: The companions learned from his state
outline.gist: A glance, a touch or a sitting with the Prophet transformed people more than his words.

outline.heading: The rabbi who saw his face and believed
outline.gist: Abdullah ibn Salam prepared questions with his son to expose him, but on seeing the Prophet's face declared it was not the face of a liar and accepted Islam.

outline.heading: More beautiful than the full moon
outline.gist: A companion looked back and forth between the full moon and the Prophet's face and found his face lovelier; those who wished misguidance stayed unaffected.

outline.heading: Recitation of the passage
outline.gist: He reads the verses on the hidden reward, believer and sinner, and the lesser punishment.

outline.heading: No soul knows the delight hidden for them
outline.gist: We know only broad headings of paradise; its realities are known only on entering, as the hadith of what no eye has seen explains.

outline.heading: The highest reward: seeing His face
outline.gist: The highest people of paradise see Allah's face morning and evening and wait for nothing else; this love is the goal of all religious learning.

outline.heading: 'I become his hearing and sight' understood through love
outline.gist: The metaphor of the hadith qudsi only makes sense as love, in which one's soul blends with the beloved's pleasure and displeasure.

outline.heading: 'A reward for what they did': honouring them
outline.gist: Though no one enters paradise by deeds, Allah attributes it to their work so they feel they deserve their place.

outline.heading: The believer and the sinner are not equal
outline.gist: One connected to his Lord cannot be treated like one who turned away.

outline.heading: Gardens of refuge and a fire with no escape
outline.gist: The believers settle in a final abode with no further departure; the sinners are returned every time they try to leave.

outline.heading: Why 'which you denied' is masculine here
outline.gist: Only here does the pronoun refer to the punishment rather than the fire, because the next verse continues about punishment; a tip for memorisers.

outline.heading: The lesser punishment: worldly hardship
outline.gist: Illness, loss and suffering are slight beside the punishment of the hereafter; equating worldly persecution with Allah's punishment is a mark of weak faith.

outline.heading: So that they may return
outline.gist: Hardship wakes people; pampered, comfortable people in wealthy countries often never think of Allah until a loss or illness brings them back.

outline.heading: 'Short of the greater': Allah wants to spare them
outline.gist: The lesser punishment is meant to make the greater unnecessary; the oath to fill hell means only with those who choose disbelief, not that it must be filled.

outline.heading: Every trial is an invitation to come closer
outline.gist: Do not let a hardship pass without returning to Allah; the sick are nearest to Him, and calamities expiate sins until one meets Him sinless.

outline.heading: Outro

32:10.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ أَءِذَا ضَلَلۡنَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَءِنَّا لَفِي خَلۡقࣲ جَدِيدِۭۚ بَلۡ هُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّهِمۡ كَٰفِرُونَ

32:11.ar: ۞قُلۡ يَتَوَفَّىٰكُم مَّلَكُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ ٱلَّذِي وُكِّلَ بِكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ تُرۡجَعُونَ

32:12.ar: وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ نَاكِسُواْ رُءُوسِهِمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ رَبَّنَآ أَبۡصَرۡنَا وَسَمِعۡنَا فَٱرۡجِعۡنَا نَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحًا إِنَّا مُوقِنُونَ
32:12.en: Couldst thou but see when the guilty hang their heads before their Lord, (and say): Our Lord! We have now seen and heard, so send us back; we will do right, now we are sure

32:13.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَأٓتَيۡنَا كُلَّ نَفۡسٍ هُدَىٰهَا وَلَٰكِنۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ مِنِّي لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ

32:14.ar: فَذُوقُواْ بِمَا نَسِيتُمۡ لِقَآءَ يَوۡمِكُمۡ هَٰذَآ إِنَّا نَسِينَٰكُمۡۖ وَذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ

IvQEPPSFOPs.speaker: adnan
IvQEPPSFOPs.speaker_note: the sheikh's Sunday Arabic tafsir; he mentions teaching seerah in London and running the masjid's youth programmes
IvQEPPSFOPs.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat As-Sajdah (verses 10-16)
IvQEPPSFOPs.one_line: Love of Allah is the top priority; the deniers who 'forgot' the meeting with Allah, free choice, the Prophet's longing for the Highest Companion, and the verse of prostration.
IvQEPPSFOPs.summary: He starts by arguing that a preacher must balance topics as the Quran does, because religious discourse that fixates on beards, qibla angles or innovation produces people who cannot rank priorities. At the top of the scale is the heart's attachment to Allah: memorising Quran without love achieves little, an empty heart cannot sustain obedience, and parents without a real relationship with their teenagers lose them to screens and drugs. Masjid programmes exist only to make children love the masjid, the Quran, the Prophet and Allah, which needs parents to come in too. Reviewing verses 10-14, he reads the surah as a reproach: Allah draws near faster than we approach, yet the deniers stand with bowed heads asking to return. Allah could have forced guidance, but reward needs a real choice. 'Forgetting' the meeting is chosen neglect, like a spouse's excuse, and Allah answers neglect with neglect. Seeing death as meeting Allah changes life; the Prophet chose the Highest Companion at the peak of his success. He covers the fiqh and dua of the prostration of recitation, then verses 15-16: hearts that fall in prostration, abundant praise without arrogance, and sides that cannot rest in bed out of longing.

outline.heading: The surah's aim: binding the heart to Allah
outline.gist: Allah began the relationship with creation and gifts out of love, so the effort now falls on the servant.

outline.heading: Balance in religious discourse
outline.gist: A speaker must balance the Shariah's commands and aims; he ties his sessions to the Quran because it covers everything proportionately, while local discourse is shaped by politics, war and poverty.

outline.heading: Inflating secondary issues
outline.gist: Some reduce Islam to beards, qibla deviations or labelling innovators; these are part of the deen but far smaller than they are made.

outline.heading: Ranking priorities: what is small and what is great
outline.gist: The slander of Aisha was treated as trivial though grave with Allah; disputed details are forgiven while morals and obligations are non-negotiable.

outline.heading: Nothing outranks loving Allah
outline.gist: He spends most of his Quran circle talking with students, because memorisation with perfect tajweed means little if the heart is not filled with love.

outline.heading: An empty heart cannot sustain obedience
outline.gist: Without attachment one prays one day and stops the next; parents who built no relationship with their children are not obeyed once they are teenagers.

outline.heading: Competing with screens, drugs and temptation
outline.gist: A frowning, forbidding approach loses to attractive distractions; he has taught the seerah in London four times to the same handful of people.

outline.heading: The real goal of masjid programmes: love
outline.gist: Volunteers exhaust themselves so that a child comes to love the masjid, then the Quran, then Allah; memorisation by all is not the aim.

outline.heading: Parents must come inside
outline.gist: A child dropped off while the parent waits in the car will not love the masjid; he needs to see his father pray and make dua.

outline.heading: Recap: ingratitude and denial of the meeting
outline.gist: After all He did, people do not thank Him and deny they will be raised; they dislike meeting Allah, yet the meeting is unavoidable.

outline.heading: The criminals with bowed heads ask to return
outline.gist: They echo the hearing and sight they were given and now claim certainty, but the time for that has passed.

outline.heading: The surah as a continuous reproach
outline.gist: The passage flows without breaks from His speech to His creation to our ingratitude and denial, like a loving reproach.

outline.heading: Draw near a span and He draws near an arm's length
outline.gist: The hadith qudsi shows Allah responds to any effort with far more.

outline.heading: Obligations first, then voluntary acts until He loves you
outline.gist: The most beloved approach is the clear obligations; voluntary acts like sunnah prayers or attending a study circle bring His love, so one hears, sees and walks by Allah.

outline.heading: All learning aims at love: from the teacher to the Prophet to Allah
outline.gist: A child first loves his teacher, who ties him to the Prophet, who leads him to Allah; the sweetness of faith is all forms of love.

outline.heading: Recitation of the next passage
outline.gist: He reads the verses on guidance, hellfire and forgetting the meeting.

outline.heading: Had We willed, every soul would be guided
outline.gist: Allah could have made people like angels; His word is that He gives them a choice and fills hell from those who choose misguidance.

outline.heading: Allah does not want to punish
outline.gist: Hell is fuel for those who insist on wrongdoing; Allah would not punish those who are grateful and believe.

outline.heading: Reward requires a real alternative
outline.gist: Rewarding someone for not breathing underwater would be meaningless; disobedience must be possible for obedience to be rewarded.

outline.heading: The gravity of sin lies in whom you disobey
outline.gist: Every human errs; whoever knows Allah's rank returns quickly, and the doors of repentance stay open.

outline.heading: 'Because you forgot': forgetting as chosen neglect
outline.gist: Genuine forgetting is forgiven, but forgetting what you never cared about is negligence, like a child who always 'forgot' the task you set.

outline.heading: 'I forgot' in marriages and on the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: The same excuse breeds conflict between spouses; the criminals' plea is rejected because they built no relationship.

outline.heading: Death as the meeting with Allah
outline.gist: Our souls are His breath and the covenant is in our nature; prayer and reading His Book are partial meetings completed at death and on the Day.

outline.heading: The Prophet chose the Highest Companion
outline.gist: Offered more life, he chose his Lord; loving to meet Allah is not about disliking death, which everyone does, as he explained to Aisha.

outline.heading: The fevers of early Madinah
outline.gist: The Prophet, Abu Bakr and Bilal fell ill, Bilal longed for Makkah in verse, and the Prophet prayed that Madinah be made beloved and healthy.

outline.heading: At the peak of success he still chose Allah
outline.gist: Healthy, respected and ruling Arabia, the Prophet told a trembling Bedouin he was the son of a woman who ate dried meat; even then he did not hesitate to choose the next life.

outline.heading: 'We have forgotten you': neglect answered with neglect
outline.gist: As they ignored the One who created and gave, they are ignored and taste lasting punishment.

outline.heading: Recitation with the prostration
outline.gist: He recites the verse of prostration and the congregation prostrates.

outline.heading: Fiqh of the prostration of recitation
outline.gist: Schools differ on wudu and takbir; one known dua is that his face prostrated to the One who created it and opened its hearing and sight.

outline.heading: A dua for the prostration of recitation
outline.gist: He recommends memorising the dua asking Allah to record reward, remove a burden and accept it as He accepted it from Dawud.

outline.heading: Obligatory or recommended: the schools' positions
outline.gist: Shafi'is end it with salam; Abu Hanifa held it obligatory, to be made up after travel, while others consider it recommended.

outline.heading: Interlude
Those whose hearts fall in prostration
outline.gist: Most commentators read it as the heart humbling itself when reminded of Allah, with self-blame and acknowledging His favour, not necessarily the body.

outline.heading: Abundant praise and no arrogance
outline.gist: Glorifying with praise means praising Him much, the opposite of 'little do you thank'; prostration, praise and lack of arrogance are the three traits.

outline.heading: Sides that cannot rest in bed
outline.gist: Tajafi is the opposite of meeting: the lover of Allah cannot settle in bed; the Prophet rose repeatedly at night and told Aisha he wanted to be a grateful servant.

outline.heading: Imams should not avoid the verses of prostration
outline.gist: Surahs like Al-Alaq and Al-Inshiqaq are rarely heard because imams avoid prostrations, though these verses are among the Quran's greatest; an imam may also recite without prostrating.

outline.heading: Outro

YsJp9RWQGLY.title: Growing Up in the Digital Age: A Talk for Parents
YsJp9RWQGLY.one_line: Dr. Jibran Khokhar weighs the benefits and harms of internet use for youth: brain development, predators, social comparison, algorithms, AI, and a family safety plan.
YsJp9RWQGLY.summary: Dr. Jibran Khokhar, a researcher on addiction, starts from the Islamic principle that things are permissible unless proven otherwise and, following the Quran's stepwise approach to alcohol, weighs the benefits of being online against its harms. Like the tobacco industry, platforms target the young because the adolescent brain's reward accelerator outpaces its frontal brake until about 25. He cites teens online most of the day, underage use, parental involvement as the strongest protection, and stressed parents using devices as a relief valve. He describes real community cases of pornography breaking marriages, online gambling begun through a streamer, predators on Roblox and Discord, and local arrests, insisting the community stop treating these as someone else's problem. Two hours a day of social media at 10 to 14 is linked to anxiety, depression and eating disorders, driven by upward comparison that the Prophet's advice to look at those below you counters. Algorithms curate a partial religion and unrealistic images of marriage, and AI chatbots flatter users. He recommends modelling restraint, cutting screen time weekly before Ramadan, router controls, private information, no devices at meals or in rooms, calm non-judgmental responses to disclosures, reporting predators, and normalizing help-seeking.

w5vA-DpEYHM.speaker: adnan

w5vA-DpEYHM.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 26 (Q&A)
w5vA-DpEYHM.one_line: Q&A on mortality: the 'last week' exercise, why deeds never make you ready, living in the moment, and why knowledge and family come first.
w5vA-DpEYHM.summary: He sets a reflection for the break: if you had one week to live, which big themes of your life would change? The righteous answered that they would change nothing, because they had already chosen the most beneficial path. Answers such as quitting work or school, or leaving for Palestine, reveal confused priorities; usually the action is right and the intention or attitude needs fixing, and leisure with good intention is itself worship. He then answers three questions. First, deeds are never enough and were never meant to be; preparation means staying on the path with hope in Allah's mercy and fear of one's shortcomings, as Imam Ahmad showed by refusing to feel safe even while dying. A healthy level of anxiety keeps people sharp. Second, living in the moment flows from grasping mortality, since time and value are defined only by their ending and by opposites. Third, he explains why seeking knowledge and providing for family top a young Muslim's priorities, citing the inheritors of the prophets, the man carrying wood counted as striving in Allah's path, and the Prophet sending companions' wealth back to their families. He adds that any beneficial field studied with the right intention counts, including behind-the-scenes work.

outline.heading: Opening
Tazkiyah never asks you to believe a lie
outline.gist: Neither 'I die this week' nor 'I live to 85' is true; any teaching that requires self-deception points to an unresolved problem.

outline.heading: From fear to preparation
outline.gist: The truth is that death could come at any moment though you will likely live long; that truth should move you from helpless fear to preparation.

outline.heading: The break exercise: would the big themes change?
outline.gist: Ignore farewells and small changes; the scholars said they would change nothing because they had already chosen what was most beneficial.

outline.heading: Quitting school or work reveals confused priorities
outline.gist: If going to Palestine or quitting is better, why wait? In youth nothing beats study, and nothing beats providing halal income for family.

outline.heading: When nothing you do has value
outline.gist: A man who would divorce his wife and quit everything is living a sad life; either change the action or change the intention.

outline.heading: Leisure as worship
outline.gist: Rest and time with friends done with the right intention prevent burnout; the Prophet had private family leisure, though his deepest rest was in prayer.

outline.heading: Fix the action or fix the intention
outline.gist: Drop work that is truly bad, otherwise change your attitude; Allah placed you where you are, so fulfil that role well.

outline.heading: Studying only for money
outline.gist: A plumber earns more per hour than he does after 286 exams; if money is your only intention, fix it or change your field before you are decades in.

outline.heading: Interlude
Q1: deeds were never designed to be enough
outline.gist: Not even the Prophet could say he had done enough; we act to please Allah hoping He makes us worthy of His mercy.

outline.heading: Relying on deeds is a sign of failure
outline.gist: You are better off when your heart is more connected and your urge to do good is stronger, not when your tally is higher.

outline.heading: Preparation is staying on the path
outline.gist: Being ready means not losing hope or faith and still trying to come closer, held between hope in His generosity and fear over one's shortcomings.

outline.heading: The truthful statement about your outcome
outline.gist: You will most likely qualify for His mercy because of Him, not you, but bad deeds could still put you in the wrong place.

outline.heading: Imam Ahmad's 'not yet'
outline.gist: Dying, he kept saying 'not yet' to Shaytan, who claimed he had escaped him, because he would not feel safe while still alive.

outline.heading: Never carefree until both feet are in Paradise
outline.gist: Live between the encouraging reality of who Allah is and the reality of your own conduct, which still needs work.

outline.heading: A healthy amount of anxiety
outline.gist: Employees with no consequences slack off and an Arabic proverb says the fearless become rude; balance is needed without ulcers or carelessness.

outline.heading: Near-death unmasks what matters
outline.gist: Facing death makes every other worry worthless; do that reflection now because sometimes it is not a near miss but the end.

outline.heading: Q2: living in the moment starts with mortality
outline.gist: Asking for other tips avoids the most effective method; mortality is what gives time its value.

outline.heading: Time and value are defined by opposites
outline.gist: He guesses time would never have been conceived without death; sweetness, health and life are known only through their opposites.

outline.heading: Cherish this half hour
outline.gist: Truly accepting you may not walk out tonight makes you cherish the people, the intention and the beauty around you.

outline.heading: Why near-death joy wears off
outline.gist: The euphoria fades unless your mental programming changes; the Prophet told us to remember the destroyer of pleasures often.

outline.heading: Remembering death balances the soul
outline.gist: It lightens hardship and restrains carefree excess, keeping happiness and sadness from becoming extreme.

outline.heading: Q3: you must care about your own hereafter
outline.gist: An imam's job is to explain priorities, not to make people care; as a physician he had to learn the same with patients choosing unproven remedies.

outline.heading: The broken fatwa relationship
outline.gist: People should seek the best choice while the scholar reassures them the easier valid option is fine, not the reverse of hunting for loopholes.

outline.heading: Knowledge: the inheritance of the prophets
outline.gist: Prophets left knowledge, not wealth; angels lower their wings for the student and nothing outranks learning in one's youth.

outline.heading: The scholar over the worshipper, and priorities by stage of life
outline.gist: The learned stand above the ignorant worshipper like the full moon over stars; the ummah needs every field, but a father must not abandon his family to study.

outline.heading: Providing for family counts as striving in Allah's path
outline.gist: When companions wished a strong man carrying wood were fighting instead, the Prophet said leaving home to support oneself, family or parents is in Allah's path.

outline.heading: Youth is the time to learn, not earn
outline.gist: Teenagers want money and older people want to quit; changing convictions and learning gets harder with age.

outline.heading: Keep some wealth for your family
outline.gist: The Prophet sent companions' donations partly back home; Abu Bakr gave everything, and his blind father was reassured by pebbles jingled in the money box.

outline.heading: Interlude
Any beneficial knowledge counts, including unseen work
outline.gist: Almost every field studied with the right intention benefits people; behind-the-scenes work can earn more because intention stays purer.

16:1.ar: أَتَىٰٓ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَسۡتَعۡجِلُوهُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
16:1.en: The commandment of Allah will come to pass, so seek not ye to hasten it. Glorified and Exalted be He above all that they associate (with Him)

16:2.ar: يُنَزِّلُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ بِٱلرُّوحِ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِۦ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦٓ أَنۡ أَنذِرُوٓاْ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱتَّقُونِ
16:2.en: He sendeth down the angels with the Spirit of His command unto whom He will of His bondmen, (saying): Warn mankind that there is no Allah save Me, so keep your duty unto Me

16:3.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ تَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
16:3.en: He hath created the heavens and the earth with truth. High be He Exalted above all that they associate (with Him)

16:4.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
16:4.en: He hath created man from a drop of fluid, yet behold! he is an open opponent

16:5.ar: وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمَ خَلَقَهَاۖ لَكُمۡ فِيهَا دِفۡءࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ وَمِنۡهَا تَأۡكُلُونَ
16:5.en: And the cattle hath He created, whence ye have warm clothing and uses, and whereof ye eat

16:6.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسۡرَحُونَ
16:6.en: And wherein is beauty for you, when ye bring them home, and when ye take them out to pasture

16:7.ar: وَتَحۡمِلُ أَثۡقَالَكُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَلَدࣲ لَّمۡ تَكُونُواْ بَٰلِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ ٱلۡأَنفُسِۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمۡ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
16:7.en: And they bear your loads for you unto a land ye could not reach save with great trouble to yourselves. Lo! your Lord is Full of Pity, Merciful

16:8.ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةࣰۚ وَيَخۡلُقُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
16:8.en: And horses and mules and asses (hath He created) that ye may ride them, and for ornament. And He createth that which ye know not

16:9.ar: وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصۡدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمِنۡهَا جَآئِرࣱۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَهَدَىٰكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
16:9.en: And Allah's is the direction of the way, and some (roads) go not straight. And had He willed He would have led you all aright

16:10.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰۖ لَّكُم مِّنۡهُ شَرَابࣱ وَمِنۡهُ شَجَرࣱ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ
16:10.en: He it is Who sendeth down water from the sky, whence ye have drink, and whence are trees on which ye send your beasts to pasture

16:11.ar: يُنۢبِتُ لَكُم بِهِ ٱلزَّرۡعَ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلنَّخِيلَ وَٱلۡأَعۡنَٰبَ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
16:11.en: Therewith He causeth crops to grow for you, and the olive and the date-palm and grapes and all kinds of fruit. Lo! herein is indeed a portent for people who reflect

16:12.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ وَٱلنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّرَٰتُۢ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
16:12.en: And He hath constrained the night and the day and the sun and the moon to be of service unto you, and the stars are made subservient by His command. Lo! herein indeed are portents for people who have sense

16:13.ar: وَمَا ذَرَأَ لَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُخۡتَلِفًا أَلۡوَٰنُهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَذَّكَّرُونَ
16:13.en: And whatsoever He hath created for you in the earth of divers hues, lo! therein is indeed a portent for people who take heed

16:14.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي سَخَّرَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ لِتَأۡكُلُواْ مِنۡهُ لَحۡمࣰ ا طَرِيࣰّ ا وَتَسۡتَخۡرِجُواْ مِنۡهُ حِلۡيَةࣰ تَلۡبَسُونَهَاۖ وَتَرَى ٱلۡفُلۡكَ مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِ وَلِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
16:14.en: And He it is Who hath constrained the sea to be of service that ye eat fresh meat from thence, and bring forth from thence ornaments which ye wear. And thou seest the ships ploughing it that ye (mankind) may seek of His bounty and that haply ye may give thanks

16:15.ar: وَأَلۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَوَٰسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمۡ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣰ ا وَسُبُلࣰ ا لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
16:15.en: And He hath cast into the earth firm hills that it quake not with you, and streams and roads that ye may find a way

16:16.en: And landmarks (too), and by the star they find a way

16:17.ar: أَفَمَن يَخۡلُقُ كَمَن لَّا يَخۡلُقُۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
16:17.en: Is He then Who createth as him who createth not? Will ye not then remember

16:18.ar: وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَةَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
16:18.en: And if ye would count the favour of Allah ye cannot reckon it. Lo! Allah is indeed Forgiving, Merciful

6:95.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَالِقُ ٱلۡحَبِّ وَٱلنَّوَىٰۖ يُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡحَيَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمَيِّتِ وَمُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡمَيِّتِ مِنَ ٱلۡحَيِّۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤۡفَكُونَ
6:95.en: Lo! Allah (it is) Who splitteth the grain of corn and the date-stone (for sprouting). He bringeth forth the living from the dead, and is the bringer-forth of the dead from the living. Such is Allah. How then are ye perverted

6:99.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مِنۡهُ خَضِرࣰ ا نُّخۡرِجُ مِنۡهُ حَبࣰّ ا مُّتَرَاكِبࣰ ا وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخۡلِ مِن طَلۡعِهَا قِنۡوَانࣱ دَانِيَةࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣲ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَابࣲ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُشۡتَبِهࣰ ا وَغَيۡرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍۗ ٱنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثۡمَرَ وَيَنۡعِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكُمۡ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:99.en: He it is Who sendeth down water from the sky, and therewith We bring forth buds of every kind; We bring forth the green blade from which We bring forth the thick-clustered grain; and from the date-palm, from the pollen thereof, spring pendant bunches; and (We bring forth) gardens of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, alike and unlike. Look upon the fruit thereof, when they bear fruit, and upon its ripening. Lo! herein verily are portents for a people who believe

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

tgKLZnOjeJI.title: Listening to the Divine: An-Nahl 1-18
tgKLZnOjeJI.one_line: New Year khutbah on An-Nahl 1-18: be grateful for the basic blessings everyone shares, and take stewardship of the planet seriously.
tgKLZnOjeJI.summary: A New Year's Day khutbah on the opening of Surat An-Nahl (16:1-18), the passage that lists the basic blessings of creation. He begins with a diagnosis: every long-lived ideology tunes out its own basics through repetition, and Muslims, once at the front of ethics and science, now spend countless hours on the one percent of details that divide them and change no behaviour, while verses like these are skimmed. The surah opens by saying Allah's command is on its way, then moves from the drop that becomes an argumentative human to livestock and the camel, freedom of choice, rain, crops, sun, moon and stars (his cosmic iPad), the sea and the mountains, ending with the reminder that His blessings cannot be counted. His main point is that the Quran rarely asks gratitude for complex blessings such as career and family; it asks for the shared basics everyone has, and the Arabic second khutbah warns that tying gratitude to complex blessings risks losing gratitude altogether. Gratitude should become a lifestyle that makes you humble, kind and motivated. His second new-year point is that no scripture is greener than the Quran, which makes Muslims stewards of a planet that can meet our needs but not our greed, a duty our countries and communities neglect.

outline.heading: Opening
Recitation of the passage
outline.gist: He recites An-Nahl 1 to 9, from the command of Allah that has come to the straight path that rests with Allah.

outline.heading: The verses we tune out
outline.gist: Verses on what Allah expects of our lives appear so often that we tune them out; any ideology that lasts long enough loses its basics through repetition.

outline.heading: From the front of history to forgetting the basics
outline.gist: Within a century or so of its arrival Islam changed the world demographically and geopolitically, and Muslims stood at the front of ethics, morality, science and knowledge before slowly tuning their basics out.

outline.heading: The one percent under a NASA lens
outline.gist: We became fixated on the small margin of details Muslims differ on across the globe, magnified like an instrument at NASA until trivial issues look astronomically large.

outline.heading: Debates that change no behaviour
outline.gist: Countless hours online and in masajid go to arguing topics that have no impact on how Muslims act, their ethics or values, except dividing them. Verses like these bring us back to what the whole story is about.

outline.heading: Allah's command is on its way: do not rush it
outline.gist: Everything will come at its decreed time, set in motion long ago and seen through to the end; He is exalted above what they associate, and the angels bring the warning that there is no god but Him, so beware.

outline.heading: The drop that argues with God
outline.gist: The heavens and earth were created in truth, and the human made from a drop becomes an open disputant, looking up to scream at God: why this ruling, why so much work, why pain, why death?

outline.heading: Livestock and the camel
outline.gist: Livestock give warmth, milk, meat, skins and bones. The camel is the most unique animal on the planet: it takes you through impossible desert, carries water and fat inside it and goes into battle, with beauty when you bring them home and send them out.

outline.heading: Loads to lands you could not reach
outline.gist: They carry your loads to places you could only reach with great hardship; horses, mules and donkeys to ride and as adornment, and He creates what you do not know.

outline.heading: Choice: had He willed He would have guided all
outline.gist: The straight path rests with Allah and some paths deviate; He could have forced everyone, but then there would be no freedom of choice. He sends down water for drink and for pasture.

outline.heading: Rain, shade and fruit
outline.gist: From the water come green and trees to walk among, shade to sit under and fruit to eat, crops, olives, palms and grapes: a sign for people who reflect.

outline.heading: The Quran rarely asks gratitude for complex blessings
outline.gist: We miss the bigger picture and take what is in front of us for granted. Status, car, office, spouse and children are complex blessings; the Quran points back to mules, donkeys and horses.

outline.heading: Just be grateful for the basics
outline.gist: You were a drop and now you are human; without domesticated animals the race would have gone nowhere; remember the rain and what it brings from the earth. Be grateful for the basics and everything else becomes extraordinary.

outline.heading: Sun, moon and stars subjected
outline.gist: Night, day, sun, moon and stars are subjected by His command, signs for those with basic reason; people struggle to be grateful for complicated things while the Quran keeps pointing to the simple ones.

outline.heading: The cosmic iPad
outline.gist: The stars exist for no reason but that he can enjoy them, a cosmic iPad to look at every day; what He spread on the earth in varied colours, and the sea subjected for fresh meat.

outline.heading: The sea, ships and mountains
outline.gist: From the sea come ornaments to wear and ships cutting through it so you seek His bounty and may be grateful; He cast mountains so the earth would not shift, with rivers and paths so you find your way.

outline.heading: Blessings beyond counting
outline.gist: Landmarks and stars for guidance. Is He who creates like one who does not? If you tried to count Allah's blessings you could not; He is forgiving and merciful.

outline.heading: Read the Book as it was revealed
outline.gist: Read the Book revealed to your Prophet and reflect on it, leave the words of theologians and speakers, and listen to Allah tell you about Himself, His creation and His giving; when gratitude fills a believer's heart his character and conduct change.

outline.heading: Gratitude for the shared blessings first
outline.gist: The Quran rarely speaks of compound blessings; it speaks of those that encompass everyone and without which we would not exist. Praise Him for sun, moon, livestock, fruit, seas and mountains before your children and your job.

outline.heading: Or risk losing gratitude altogether
outline.gist: Many people wanted the complex blessings and never reached them; tie your gratitude to them and ignore the simple ones, and he fears you lose gratitude entirely. The Quran is full of verses asking thanks for the basics.

outline.heading: A moment of gratitude that becomes a lifestyle
outline.gist: Even those who never got what you have are expected to be grateful, because the basics are infinite and shared by all; start this year with a moment of gratitude that turns into a way of life.

outline.heading: Ahmad before Muhammad
outline.gist: Before he was Muhammad he was Ahmad: Allah is worthy of praise whether or not you see the reasons, and the blessings everyone shares, rich or poor, young or old, healthy or sick, change your whole perspective.

outline.heading: No book is greener than the Quran
outline.gist: No scripture he knows speaks so often of the environment and of our partnership with every living thing; the repetition gets tuned out, like the verse on Allah splitting the grain and the date stone.

outline.heading: Needs, not greed
outline.gist: Repetition is for contemplation, not confusion. We are frying a planet that can meet our needs but not our greed; no group has more reason than Muslims to be passionate about preserving it.

outline.heading: Stewards destined for the earth
outline.gist: The Quran keeps telling Muslims they are stewards responsible for the earth; before Adam was created Allah told the angels he was destined for it, and the Jannah story teaches us not to let greed guide us. Yet Muslim countries show little love for the planet.

outline.heading: The little things that are the big ones
outline.gist: Even our communities rank the environment low. For the new year: be grateful for the air, the clouds, the blue horizon and the green; this is all He ever promised, and everything else is extra time.

outline.heading: Extra time: you negotiated nothing
outline.gist: The ninety minutes are over and the referee is giving extra minutes. You had no hand in your creation and sat at no table to plan it, yet existence is breathtaking; what are you ignoring?

outline.heading: Gratitude makes you humble, kind and motivated
outline.gist: Gratitude makes you empathetic and pushes you to give back and take responsibility, for yourselves and the planet, so the ummah might turn a corner; he prays the young generation carries this beyond itself.

outline.heading: Outro

9:38.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَا لَكُمۡ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمُ ٱنفِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱثَّاقَلۡتُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا مِنَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۚ فَمَا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ
9:38.en: O ye who believe! What aileth you that when it is said unto you: Go forth in the way of Allah, ye are bowed down to the ground with heaviness. Take ye pleasure in the life of the world rather than in the Hereafter? The comfort of the life of the world is but little in the Hereafter

9:39.ar: إِلَّا تَنفِرُواْ يُعَذِّبۡكُمۡ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا وَيَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ وَلَا تَضُرُّوهُ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
9:39.en: If ye go not forth He will afflict you with a painful doom, and will choose instead of you a folk other than you. Ye cannot harm Him at all. Allah is Able to do all things

9:40.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدۡ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ إِذۡ هُمَا فِي ٱلۡغَارِ إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودࣲ لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلسُّفۡلَىٰۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلۡعُلۡيَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
9:40.en: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise

9:41.ar: ٱنفِرُواْ خِفَافࣰ ا وَثِقَالࣰ ا وَجَٰهِدُواْ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُمۡ وَأَنفُسِكُمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
9:41.en: Go forth, light-armed and heavy-armed, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of Allah! That is best for you if ye but knew

9:42.ar: لَوۡ كَانَ عَرَضࣰ ا قَرِيبࣰ ا وَسَفَرࣰ ا قَاصِدࣰ ا لَّٱتَّبَعُوكَ وَلَٰكِنۢ بَعُدَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلشُّقَّةُۚ وَسَيَحۡلِفُونَ بِٱللَّهِ لَوِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡنَا لَخَرَجۡنَا مَعَكُمۡ يُهۡلِكُونَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّهُمۡ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
9:42.en: Had it been a near adventure and an easy journey they had followed thee, but the distance seemed too far for them. Yet will they swear by Allah (saying): If we had been able we would surely have set out with you. They destroy their souls, and Allah knoweth that they verily are liars

Rs2xIFtlFHI.speaker: adnan
Rs2xIFtlFHI.speaker_note: His own tafsir series; speaks as a Canadian imam who fears Bill C-9 could stop him quoting these verses.
Rs2xIFtlFHI.title: Listening to the Divine: At-Tawbah 38-43
Rs2xIFtlFHI.one_line: Tabuk and the cave: mobilize whatever you have, Allah needs no one, courage at your lowest point, and no insurance policy with God.
Rs2xIFtlFHI.summary: A year-end khutbah on At-Tawbah 38-42, the verses revealed when the Prophet called the people out to Tabuk. He opens with a warning about Bill C-9, which he fears could make quoting Quranic verses prosecutable and which he says targets Muslims without consultation with imams, and urges people to write to their MPs. Tabuk came at the worst time, a thousand kilometres north in August when exhausted people needed their harvest, and for once the Prophet named the destination openly; the mixed response drew the rebuke of 9:38. He reads infiru as mobilize whatever you have, physician, lawyer or programmer, and hears the heaviness of iththaqaltum in the word itself. Allah needs no one; you mobilize for your own record. Then 9:40 takes him to the hijrah: perfectly planned, yet the pursuers reached the very cave, and the Prophet said not do not fear but do not be sad, because they had done everything they could and Allah was with them. The moment that defines you is at the bottom of the valley, still standing. The second khutbah on 9:41-42 condemns those who would come for a short profitable trip but not for a lifetime of effort: there is no insurance policy with Allah, go all in, and may the new year bring that courage.

outline.heading: Opening
Recitation of the passage
outline.gist: He recites At-Tawbah 38 to 40, from clinging heavily to the earth to the word of Allah being highest.

outline.heading: Bill C-9 and the freedom to quote the Quran
outline.gist: Listen to Allah, who began the conversation. He chose these verses fearing the government may soon bar him from quoting them: the bill could label Quranic words as prohibited speech, will be used on Muslims alone, and was advanced without consulting the community or its imams, another attempt to restrict their liberty.

outline.heading: Every end is a beginning
outline.gist: The verses suit the end of the year, more properly the hijri year; noticing that something has ended invites reflection on what to do better with the days, months or whatever time remains.

outline.heading: Tabuk: a second round with the Romans
outline.gist: The first round at Mu'tah ended in a strategic retreat counted as a victory; now the emperor in the north had massed troops and allies, and the Prophet chose to meet them in the north rather than let them march toward Madinah.

outline.heading: The worst possible timing
outline.gist: Like a Friday when weather and work make you wonder whether to come, and you would be excused; but this was a matter of the security of the deen and the nation.

outline.heading: He always concealed his destination
outline.gist: The Prophet never revealed where he was heading, even misdirecting his own army: positioned east, scouts sent west, while he was going south all along, so no one would worry and no secret could leak.

outline.heading: Except Tabuk: the destination named openly
outline.gist: A thousand kilometres north in mid-August, when people were poor, sick and exhausted and needed the dates on their trees; the response was mixed and the Quran answered almost immediately.

outline.heading: Infiru: mobilize whatever you have
outline.gist: To go forth means get up and move with whatever you do: physician, lawyer, teacher, driver, the programmer with his laptop. Bring what you know how to do.

outline.heading: The heaviness of clinging to the earth
outline.gist: Iththaqaltum carries its heaviness in its very sound, audible even to non-Arabic speakers. When the call says all hands on deck tomorrow morning, suddenly your back hurts and your body cannot lift off the ground.

outline.heading: Satisfied with this life over the next?
outline.gist: Clinging to the earth means something of this world attracts you more than the Hereafter; yet the enjoyment of this life, set against the next, is little.

outline.heading: He will replace you; you harm Him nothing
outline.gist: If you do not go forth He will punish you and bring another people, and you will not harm Him at all. You do this for you; no one does Allah a favour by mobilizing.

outline.heading: Allah is not begging
outline.gist: Whenever He asks for something heavy He reminds you not to imagine He needs you; you bear the consequences of your choice either way, and He is giving you an opportunity to put on your record for the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Allah aided him when none of you were there
outline.gist: If you do not support him, Allah already did, many times, when the disbelievers drove him out, the second of two in the cave with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, telling him do not be sad.

outline.heading: Had he been caught, the story would have ended
outline.gist: There was not yet enough momentum and much of the revelation had not come; had the hijrah failed there would have been no later victories or conquests.

outline.heading: The moment that matters most
outline.gist: It is not the hilltop but the bottom of the valley, when you are still on your feet, still standing and still mobilizing, though you cannot see any light at the end of the tunnel.

outline.heading: The hijrah planned to perfection
outline.gist: Your legacy is how you behaved at your lowest. The camels waited outside, he left at midnight with Ali in his bed after weeks of sleeping there at that hour, a shepherd's flock covered the tracks, they went south for three days to a remote cave and sent the camels away.

outline.heading: They reached the very cave
outline.gist: Against all odds, with no one knowing where they went, the pursuers found not the mountain or the area but the cave itself, while the two hid in a smaller hollow inside.

outline.heading: Not do not fear, but do not be sad
outline.gist: Hearing Abu Jahl and the others on the steps, they thought it was over. The Prophet did not tell Abu Bakr not to be afraid, because he did not know what would happen next; the beauty of the story is his courage.

outline.heading: We did everything we could; Allah is with us
outline.gist: Why be sad? If death comes we die on our feet doing what we were asked, with Allah pleased with us; there was no shortcoming in the plan. All the pursuers had to do was look down and see his feet.

outline.heading: The pursuers who never looked down
outline.gist: Seven or eight of them stood around and on top of the cave, one close enough to see through a small hole, yet no one looked; he imagines them later blaming each other for not checking.

outline.heading: Tranquility and unseen soldiers
outline.gist: Allah sent down His tranquility and supported him with soldiers they did not see, made the word of the disbelievers lowest and His own word the highest.

outline.heading: Interlude
A near gain and a short journey
outline.gist: Go forth light or heavy and strive with wealth and life. Had it been a quick profit a hundred kilometres away they would have come; the issue was the effort. Such people are there when it is easy but not when it takes a lifetime.

outline.heading: False oaths, and the courage to go all in
outline.gist: They swear they would have come if they could, destroying themselves, and Allah knows they lie. Do not be in for small efforts and out for big ones; mobilize all you have, which takes courage.

outline.heading: No insurance policy with Allah
outline.gist: People spread their bets like investors diversifying stocks, but with Allah there is no hedge: go all in, let the bricks fall where they may, and may the new year bring the courage he showed in the cave.

outline.heading: He decides how the story is told
outline.gist: Do not be sad, we did everything we could; if this is the end we die standing and courageous. My job is to mobilize with everything I have; He decides how the story is told, and I decide only what I did.

outline.heading: Outro
